messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a customer hit where a streaming session that got handed off between routers ended up generating provisional charge tokens on both sides, then confirmed on the second router, so the invoice shows extra short-lived tokens.

devon: ugh. do you have an example trace id? :eyes:

maya: trace=tr_9b3f — timeline: client opens stream -> router A provisions tokens -> network blip -> client reconnects to router B -> router B provisions again and consumes -> router A never revoked provisional credits because it didn't see a final ack.

sam: is this the handoff path where we allowed session transfer without explicit lease revocation? sounds like ownership race.

maya: yeah. router A thinks it still owns prefix until TTL, router B assumes new owner immediately and confirms consumption. we double-count provisional -> confirmed.

chao: what does billing ledger do today when two provisional entries exist and only one confirms? last I checked we dedupe by confirmed markers but provisional stays as noise until GC.

lisa: correct — provisional entries expire after grace window (5m) and get clipped, but our UI/console shows provisional charges under "recent" until GC which confuses customers.

devon: two problems: 1) double provisional creation on handoff, 2) provisional not cleared fast enough when another router confirms. both lead to temporary over-reporting.

sam: proposal: switch to explicit lease + revocation on handoff. client reconnect flow: new router asks old router to revoke lease via internal API w/ idempotency token. If old unreachable, new router tags provisional as "handoff-pending" and waits X ms before confirming.

maya: +1 on revocation API. but we need fallback for cases where old router crashed. waiting adds latency to user-facing reconnects. we also don't want to delay confirms for low-latency apps.

chao: alternative: optimistic confirm but emit a compensating event when we detect duplicate provisional in ledger. That requires better telemetry to link prov->confirmed across routers.

devon: how expensive is building cross-router dedupe? we need a stable session id propagated from client that survives reconnects. currently session ids are ephemeral per router.

maya: we already propagate client session-id in header `x-session-id` for some integrations. maybe standardize that for streaming handoff and use it as dedupe key.

lisa: console change: show a transient "provisional overlap" flag on recent billing widget when we detect same session id with >1 provisional within short window. Collapsing on the UI would avoid freakouts.

sam: telemetry query to find affected customers (KQL example):
```
stream_events
| where timestamp > ago(24h)
| where eventType in ("provisioned","confirmed")
| summarize makeset(router) by session_id, count()
| where array_length(makeset_router) > 1
```

chao: I ran that for last 48h, returned ~17 sessions across 3 customers, mostly on high-churn mobile networks.

devon: next steps: 1) wire `x-session-id` propagation for streaming reconnect 2) add revocation endpoint to router control API (idempotent) 3) add dedupe/compensating job in billing pipeline to collapse prov->confirmed duplicates 4) UX: provisional-overlap indicator + help text.

maya: can we implement quick mitigation in ledger: when a confirmed appears and there exists a provisional with same session_id within grace_window, mark provisional as "superseded" and remove from recent UI instantly (no full GC wait)?

chao: that seems easy — ledger already supports state transitions. prod risk is low if we only change UI visibility and not invoices. but we should not rewrite historical invoices without legal signoff.

lisa: agreed — only change UI/console visibility + billing telemetry. operations can run compensation for visible spikes if needed but invoice calculation stays as-is until legal approves automatic crediting.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-331 — "stream handoff provisional duplication" (sev3). Assigned to @devon.

devon: I'll take the API revocation + ledger supersede path. pairing with @chao for the dedupe job. ETA: PRs by EOD Wednesday.

maya: thanks. I'll draft a short console copy for the provisional-overlap flag and add to support runbook.

sam: leaving a note: we should also consider backpressure settings — pre-provisioning too aggressively increases chance of duplication. maybe throttle provisional window on reconnects.

devon: good call. will add a config flag: `reconnect_provision_backoff_ms`. default low, can be tuned per customer tier.

lisa: please post PR links here when up; we'll coordinate release with a small console rollout and a support FYI. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks everyone — keeping an eye on tr_9b3f and will update when mitigated.
